The script downloads an executable from a remote URL into the user's APPDATA (or home) and immediately executes it via subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True). Fetching a remote .exe (x69.exe) and running it without user interaction or validation is consistent with a dropper/backdoor and is deliberate malicious behavior rather than benign utility code.

The script downloads a remote executable ("Payload.exe") from a raw GitHub URL using urllib.request.urlretrieve and immediately executes it via subprocess.run with no validation, sandboxing, or user consent. This is remote code execution behavior that is characteristic of installers/droppers and is high-risk/malicious.

This code deliberately fetches and executes remote JavaScript (raw.githubusercontent.com) with a cache‑buster, and does nonstandard, wide‑ranging bridging of the parent window into the blob iframe (enumerating and defining all parent properties onto the iframe globalThis). That pattern exposes the embedding page’s internal objects to arbitrary remote code and effectively gives the fetched script full same‑origin capabilities. Loading and running third‑party code in this way (via blob iframe + property copying) is a powerful remote code execution / injection technique and is highly suspicious — it enables malicious behavior even if the remotely hosted script itself is later changed. Without clear benign context, this is malicious.
